text:
maria: Heads up — since ~03:05 UTC we're seeing ~1.2k GPU pods Pending in ap-southeast1. Most fail with 'node(s) had taints that the pod didn't tolerate' or 'Affinity rules unsatisfiable'. Nodes report healthy kubelet + GPU drivers. Any quick theories?

autoscaler-bot: Autoscaler event at 03:08 UTC — scale-up inhibited: quotaExceeded (cores) in ap-southeast1. Suggested action: request quota increase or shift workloads.

aj: I pulled kubelet logs on a couple Pending nodes — lots of NVLink attach timeouts and attach-detach backoffs. Snippet:

```
Mar 23 03:06:12 node-apse1a kubelet[1234]: E0323 03:06:12.123456  1234 cni.go:378] CNI failed to set up pod "pod-xyz": networkPlugin cni failed: failed to attach nvlink: timeout waiting for resource
Mar 23 03:06:12 node-apse1a kubelet[1234]: W0323 03:06:12.123789  1234 eviction_manager.go:265] Attempting to reclaim ephemeral resources
```

sam: This aligns with the new 'az-peer' affinity rollout — we tightened inference-prod to require same-az peers for nvlink-backed batches. Older batch jobs still point to preferredDuringScheduling which the scheduler is treating as hard because of taint+topology. So scheduler can't find nodes satisfying both taint tolerations and strict az-affinity.

emily: Can we soften the affinity for the batches temporarily? We can also evict background batch jobs in the Dedicated pools to free slots. @oncall? :thinking_face: 

oncall: I'm on it. Starting a soft-evict for low-priority batch deployments in ap-southeast1a first (will scale replicas to 0.1x during drain). ETA ~10m. Command I'm running now:

```sh
kubectl -n ml rollout pause deployment/batch-worker && kubectl scale deployment/batch-worker --replicas=20 --namespace=ml --timeout=5m
# then cordon select nodes tagged rack=nvlink-hot to test pack behavior
```

aj: Scheduler metric snapshot (03:10 UTC): binpack_efficiency_drop = 0.62 -> 0.38 over 5m, pending_gpu_pods = 1187, attach_timeout_rate = 4.3/min.

maria: Cost tradeoff question — if we bump warm-pool or provision extra on-demand r6-gpu we incur extra spend. Would you prefer transient capacity or relaxing affinity?

dana: Short-term patch: add toleration for nvlink-maintainer: true on batch jobs and set inference-prod to preferredDuringScheduling (not requiredDuring). I'll open a tiny PR to flip the affinity operator; that should allow scheduler to place ~60% of pending pods quickly. PR: https://git.internal/r/redwood/patches/1234 (wip).

infra-bot: Deployment "batch-worker" scaled by dana at 03:16 UTC. Rollout started.

aj: Quick note — if we relax affinity we may see cross-az NVLink fallback (higher latency) for some models. Metric to watch: nvlink_latency_p50 and p95.

emily: Agreed — prefer relax+evict combo for now, then follow-up with quota request for longer-term capacity.

oncall: Soft-evict completed for ap-southeast1a batches. Pack behavior improved on initial nodes, pending count dropped 1187 -> 420 in 12m. Monitoring dashboards now.

maria: Thanks all — oncall proceeding with soft-evict + dana's toleration/affinity patch. Monitor nvlink and latency dashboards. I'll follow up with a brief postmortem and a proposal: (1) stricter rollout gating for az-peer label, (2) quota bump request, (3) automated fallback to preferredDuringScheduling for 15m after scale events.

#repro_steps: check kubelet attach logs, watch autoscaler events, validate affinity semantics in scheduler traces

#notes: keep an eye on cost if we end up provisioning on-demand for >2 hours.
